content.text: A law of nature is a universal claim, like 'all metals expand when heated'. We support it with many observed cases, never all of them.

content.definition: A law says what would happen: if this were copper, it would conduct. An accidental truth says no such thing.

examples.title: From cases to a law
lines: Every metal tested so far expanded.
examples.conclusion: So all metals expand when heated.
examples.note: This is inductive: we tested some metals and concluded about all of them.

examples.title: An accidental truth
lines: All the coins in my pocket are quarters.
examples.note: It is true, but a coin would not become a quarter by being put in my pocket.

question.prompt: What sets a law of nature apart from an accidental truth?
options: A law says what would happen in other cases
question.hint: Ask what each one says about a case that is not actual.
question.explanation: A law supports claims about what would happen: if this were copper, it would conduct. An accidental truth supports no such claim.
